doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Dallas childhood, training and early playing
title: Mother's training at Wiley College; first hearing Hank Jones
summary: His mother studied music at Wiley College, took him to Jazz at the Philharmonic where he first saw Hank Jones, and he played by ear on records by Louis Jordan and Nat King Cole.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What do you know about your mother's musical training? You said she was an aspiring concert pianist.

No, she just studied piano either before I was born … I can't give you much details, but she uh, was, went to college in Texas down in … named Wiley College, and I presume she, uh, had a, uh, she, uh, she took a major in whatever music program they had. And so that's where she was sort of trained. But she had an affinity for jazz that was uncanny, I mean, uh, I mean uncanny in a sense that she would take me to concerts. That's when I first heard Hank Jones. That, that tour, Jazz at the Philharmonic, I uh, my eyes, my eyes popped when I saw Hank, you know. I was very, very single-minded, you know. I said, "Wow!" – to sum up my feelings about Mr. Jones at that time. And we had a …

Uh, I was twelve, thirteen, fourteen maybe. Maybe twelve, you know. Pretty young, but totally impressionable because I'd been trying to play since I was five, you know. There was a room in my home, in our home that uh, in winter time, they didn't turn on the heat unless we had guests, you know, so I would put on my overcoat and go in there and tinkle and play what I thought I heard on these records by Louie Jordan and Nat King Cole. And now I know I wasn't

even close, but at that time I thought I was. So … [laughs] it was like fooling myself in a way, you know? But in a good way. You know, just picking out things and making up stuff as my mother used to refer to it, but …
